title: Ground breaking held for Super Sack work
text:
THE DENISON HERALD-Thursday, December 22

TEXOMALAND

[Photograph: Large crowd of employees lined up outdoors at a groundbreaking ceremony. Several officials stand at center. Caption reads:]

Savoy Super Sack groundbreaking

The shovel of dirt flies high in the air after Super Sack Inc. President Bob Williamson tossed it at the photographers. The company officials and others, plus the 177 Super Sack employees turned out for the ground breaking for the new plant addition. At right, Super Sack Vice President Ced Derby, left, chats with Savoy Mayor James Teems at the ceremony. Story on page 1.
(Herald photos by John Clift)

Ground breaking held for Super Sack work

By JOHN CLIFT
Herald state editor

SAVOY — With 177 cheering employees in the background, top officials of Super Sack Inc. broke ground on a bright, sunny Wednesday afternoon for a major addition to the Savoy plant.

Once completed by the summer of 1989, Super Sack will start adding the first of another 100 employees.

"Right now we are one of the top three largest employers in Fa[nnin] County. By the time we co[mplete] this addition and another expansion planned in 1990, we easily should be the biggest single employer in the county," said Ced Derby, vice presi-dent of the firm.

Bob Williamson, president of the parent firm, B.A.G. Corp. of Dallas, said the 12 years Super Sack had been in operation in Savoy had been "good for the area and good for B.A.G."

Williamson said the new additions, to be added in three areas, will cover a total of 26,250 square feet to the Savoy plant. This will bring 74,750 square feet or 1.72 acres under one roof for the fast growing bag company.

In addition, in 1990 Super Sack is looking to an even larger expansion of 43,755 square feet just

east of the present building that will firmly establish the Savoy industry as the major industrial plant in Fannin County.

Williamson said the enlargement of the test building, which Williamson described as "unique in the bag business," will permit faster, more comprehensive research into how customer products may be more economically handled.

The 6,000 square foot equipment building will free up another 6,000 square feet in the main plant that can be used in fabricating the Super Sack containers, Williamson said. This will give the main plant a total of 68,750 square feet of working space.

Williamson said the biggest of the three additions will be an 18,750 foot addition to the main plant. The north wall will be removed to provide an open space into the new area.

The corporation president said that when B.A.G. opened in 1969 "the bags that we made forever changed the material handling industry. Since then, millions of tons of dry flowable materials have been handled and shipped easily and at a much lower cost in Super Sack containers."

Even though B.A.G. has copyrighted the name "Super Sack" that name has become synonymous with large shipping sacks.

"I have been known to get phone calls from some of our competion complaining that they get calls from people wanting to order some 'super sacks'," Williamson smiled.

Williamson pitched out the first shovel of dirt and later was joined by Derby and Jean Williamson, secretary-treasurer. Other officials on hand included Plant Manager Dave Kellenberger, Super Sack Vice President Webb Cox, Savoy Mayor James Teems, Small Business Administration's Marvin McPherson, Greenville builder Jim Morris, and the 177 plant employees.
